analysis.title: GS Sharkey - Earnings Playbook 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: Q3 earnings season starts next week with banks (BAC, C, JPM, MS, WFC), TMT (ASML, TSMC) and LVMH in focus. 70% of index market cap reports by late October, most hyperscalers report in the final week, and NVDA reports 11/19.
Banks have lagged the S&P 500 by about 10% over the past month going into their reports.
Consensus expects S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth of +27% y/y, the highest estimate since 2021. The median stock is at 9% y/y versus 14% in Q2.
Last quarter beats were frequent but were rewarded with only 35bps of day-1 outperformance versus the S&P, against 95bps historically. Only Q1'26, '24, '20 and '17 were worse.
Mag7 had its most volatile earnings quarter on record in Q2. Prime book positioning in Mag7 went from a YTD low of 14% of US exposure in June to a record 22%.

MU beat across the board and said supply tightness persists into 2028, but the stock reaction was muted. The note asks whether the bar is equally high across the AI complex and whether investors are hesitant to add AI exposure ahead of the midterms.

Semis: sentiment is improving on cleaner positioning, a 'consumer agent' product cycle and seasonality, but tactical risk remains after a 'beat-and-fade' Q2 season. The debate is how much upside remains without visibility into 2028+.
Current momentum is in asset-light, capex-agnostic inference plays across data infrastructure and cyber security (Callahan).
EPS growth is highly concentrated. AI infrastructure drives more than 50% of EPS growth, the top 10 stocks more than two-thirds, and MU and NVDA more than one-third.
Consensus hyperscaler capex growth is +116% y/y in Q3 versus +87% in Q2. GS expects capex to grow more than 50% in 2027, above the $1.1trn consensus, and expects little visibility on 2028.
AI return evidence: cloud revenue growth is expected at 55% in Q3 versus 48% in Q2, with large backlogs. 50% of companies discussed AI productivity last quarter but only 2% quantified the EPS impact.
Margins are expected to be flat to down sequentially at 14.7% in Q3 versus 15.1% in Q2, with input cost pressure higher. Median sales growth is 6% y/y versus 7% in Q2.
The weaker dollar added about 2pp to revenue growth in Q1 and 1pp in Q2, and adds less than 1pp in Q3.

Tech and Energy account for more than 80% of EPS growth. Breadth is weak: the index is about 2% from its all-time high while the median stock is 17% below its high, the lowest breadth since the Dot Com Bubble.
The implied average stock move for earnings is 5.4%, in line with the average of the last four quarters.

sector_views.rationale: Sentiment is improving with cleaner positioning, a consumer agent product cycle and seasonality, but beat-and-fade risk remains and there is no visibility into 2028+.
Banks lagged the S&P 500 by about 10% over the past month and lead the start of earnings season. A separate GS Fins preview is referenced.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth: consensus estimate +27% y/y (forecast), versus 33% realized in Q2 2026. This is the highest estimate since 2021.
Median stock Q3 2026 EPS growth: consensus estimate 9% y/y (forecast), versus 14% in Q2. Growth decelerates in every sector except TMT and Energy.
Q2 2026 reaction: beats outperformed the S&P by 35bps on day 1 (reported), versus 95bps historically.
MU reported a beat across the board in its latest print (reported). The stock reaction was muted.
Q3 hyperscaler capex consensus +116% y/y (forecast) versus +87% in Q2. Cloud revenue growth consensus 55% in Q3 (forecast) versus 48% in Q2.
Q3 margin consensus 14.7% versus 15.1% in Q2 (forecast). Median sales growth consensus 6% y/y versus 7% in Q2 (forecast).
Reporting calendar: banks (BAC, C, JPM, MS, WFC), ASML, TSMC and LVMH next week. Most hyperscalers in the last week of October. NVDA on 11/19.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Economists' nominal GDP growth of about 6% is the benchmark for the 6% median sales growth expected for S&P 500 companies.

risk_factors: High bar: the +27% y/y consensus is the highest since 2021, and beats are rewarded less than usual.
Beat-and-fade risk in semis and the wider AI complex, as shown by the muted MU reaction.
Record Mag7 positioning at 22% of US exposure raises crowding risk.
Extreme earnings concentration: the top 10 stocks drive more than two-thirds of EPS growth and MU plus NVDA more than one-third.
Little visibility into AI capex in 2028 and beyond.
Margin pressure from higher input costs, and a shrinking tailwind from the weaker dollar.
charts_described: Bottom-up consensus estimates show S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% year/year in Q3 2026.
Consensus estimates show hyperscaler capex growth exceeding 100% year/year in Q3.
Consensus capex estimates have consistently been too conservative in recent years.
vol_and_positioning: Mag7 positioning on the GS Prime book rose from a YTD low of 14% of US exposure in June to a record 22%.
Implied average earnings move is 5.4%, in line with the average of the last four quarters.
Market breadth is the lowest since the Dot Com Bubble. The index is about 2% below its all-time high and the median stock is 17% below its high.
Mag7 earnings in Q2 were the most volatile on record.
geopolitical: US midterm elections are cited as a source of uncertainty that may make investors hesitant to commit capital to AI trades.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth is accelerating (55% in Q3 versus 48% in Q2), backlogs are large, capex consensus is rising, and semis sentiment is improving with cleaner positioning. Momentum is in asset-light inference plays.
tension_points.bear_case: The bar is the highest since 2021, Mag7 positioning is at a record 22%, and MU's muted reaction to a full beat suggests beats are not being rewarded. Visibility into 2028+ is limited and EPS growth is extremely concentrated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Muted or negative day-1 reactions to beats from the Mag7 and hyperscalers in the last week of October would confirm the high-bar dynamic across the AI complex.

theme_stances.key_argument: Consensus EPS growth of 27% is the highest since 2021 and beats have been rewarded with the smallest outperformance on record, so the setup is demanding.
MU beat across the board with a muted reaction, raising the question of whether the bar is high across AI names.
